lots.guide_summary: $150 to $420 from close comparables only, all from one sale (Noble Sale 140, Nov 2025, the Jack Grace collection): five SOLD at $200, $250, $250, $260 and $420 (very likely hammer), and two UNSOLD (passed in at $150 and $200 estimates). No exact match (stars and green stones design) was found with a price. Category guides kept but outside the range: a 15ct Coo-ee SOLD $320, a 2015 15ct Duggin Shappere SOLD $850, and a UK dealer ASKING GBP 980 (AUD 1,863). Melt context: gold USD 4,088/oz (gold-api.com, 7 Oct 2026) at USD 1 = AUD 1.4322 is about AUD 188/g fine, so 9ct is about AUD 70.6/g; roughly 2.2-2.4g of gold is AUD 155-170 at spot, less for scrap.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD within 24 months = $200 (Noble lot 3172, Nov 2025, 2.62g). 200 / 1.198 = 166.9, round down to $165 (all-in about $198). Flip: likely resale about $250 hammer (the three plain or near-plain figural 9ct kookaburras at $250-260); less about 15% selling commission and $10 outbound postage = 250 x 0.85 - 10 = $202.50; 202.50 / 2.396 = 84.5, round down to $80. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah). Caveat: these are close comparables, not the identical design, and all from one specialist sale; Noble buyers may have paid 22% on top, which makes these figures conservative.
lots.confidence_reason: The 9ct is from the Gowans title; the three pictorial punches on the back could not be read even enlarged, so the maker is unknown. Five opened SOLD results exist, but they are close rather than identical and all from one sale. Unread mark forces Low.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: figural chased kookaburra on a branch inside two concentric wire rings, six star mounts each with a round green stone (colour and sparkle suggest paste). Photo 2 (cropped and enlarged 3x): three pseudo-hallmark punches in cut-corner cartouches, typical of Australian makers copying British marks; first looks like an animal or head shape, second a round device, third a letter or crown shape, none legible. No 9 or 9CT visible in the photographed area. Pin is copper or brass coloured, consistent with Gowans' 'gilt pin'.
lots.condition: Looks complete with all six stones present; no obvious damage visible; light surface wear to the back; pin base metal (not gold). Catch not clearly shown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm where the 9ct mark is (we can only see three pictorial punches), whether any maker's mark is visible, that all six green stones are present and secure, and that the pin and catch work?
